trophies.guide: No separate objective sits behind this one — it fires the moment the other 54 trophies are all yours. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap below: story plus the single missable first, activities and collectibles next, and the 100% gold as the final step before this pops.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: This is the game's opening mission, so expect it to be the first trophy on your list. Run the introduction to its end screen and use the quiet stretches to practise driving, on-foot movement and shaking the cops — those basics underpin every mission after it.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Work through all of Chapter 1's missions and the trophy arrives with the chapter-complete screen. Chapters must be played in sequence, so just chase the mission markers. The map is still compact here, which makes it the best chapter to start visiting meditation spots for the one missable trophy.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Clear every mission in Chapter 2. New ground opens up here and side activities start appearing — try one of each type as you pass them, since Master of None only wants a single attempt at all nine. Meditation spots are worth a stop whenever one is on your route between missions.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: See Chapter 3 through to its last mission. Mid-story is when the mission list starts branching, so after each story beat glance at what new stranger and contact missions have appeared — several of them feed trophies further down this list. It is also a sensible point to start setting money aside for garages and the spending goal.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish all of Chapter 4. These late missions run long and hit hard, so buy armour and ammunition before the big set-pieces and lean on cover — a death only sends you back to a checkpoint, never to the start of the chapter. After this one, the final mission is all that remains of the story.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Complete the last story mission. It is the longest in the game, so clear an uninterrupted session and save by hand before you begin. Free roam stays open once the credits roll, so anything unfinished — collectibles, challenges, the 100% gold — can be mopped up afterwards.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: A story mission that shows up in the list once the story reaches it — follow the marker and play it out. If it has not appeared, push the story forward: these missions unlock one after another, and the next story beat is usually what opens the door. No special gear is called for.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: A story heist mission. Heists reward going in ready: armour on, a weapon you are accurate with, and the game's own plan followed rather than improvised. The trophy lands on the mission-complete screen, and the heist payout is a handy boost for the money trophies.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: A story mission that joins the list once the story gets there. It is short with a plain objective — just play it through. If it is not offered yet, keep clearing story missions and the contact will offer it in due course.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: A story mission — start it at the marker and follow it through. It involves a lot of driving, so an upgraded fast car from your garage makes it noticeably easier. The trophy pops when the mission-complete screen appears.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: A story mission centred on the airport, with a heavy firefight at its core. Go in with full armour and a well-stocked rifle, fight from cover, and use Combat Focus to slow the tightest stretches — the same discipline the Gunslinger trophy wants.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: A late-story mission and one of the toughest fights in the game. Come prepared as for any set-piece: armour stocked, a shotgun for close work, a rifle for distance, and your partner used as a distraction when the game offers the choice. The trophy unlocks when the mission ends.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Push the in-game completion stat to 100% — the final gold before the platinum. The stat rolls up story missions, stranger strands, activities, collectibles and challenges, so there is no separate grind hiding behind it: finish everything else and this follows. The stats menu shows which category is still short; chase that list. Story and the missable come first, so the endgame is counting rather than replaying.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Jumps, near misses and long airtime all feed this counter, and it runs for the whole game, so ordinary driving already moves it. For a focused grind, pick one jump or ramp you can hit over and over in a fast car and loop it — every clean landing with airtime adds one. Two hundred and fifty sounds steep, but a single dedicated ramp session with a good spot burns through it.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: One go at each of the 9 activity types is all it takes — attempt, not win. The types are the ones listed in the game's activities menu: races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade games, drone races and the rest. Work down that list one item at a time and the trophy fires on the ninth. Best done early, while you are getting to know the map anyway.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Take gold in every one of the 42 Shooting Range challenges. Each has a score bar for gold, and precision beats speed: spend the extra half-second on headshots, fire in short bursts to manage recoil, and learn a range's layout before chasing its gold run. Shoot with the weapon the challenge hands you, and retry one challenge at a time — each one saves its own progress, so clear them individually.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. These races are won on clean lines rather than raw speed: trim the corners where the course allows it, dodge the obstacles that spin you out, and take a slow first lap to learn a course before racing it for real. The locations are scattered across Leonida, so knock them out while travelling for the exploration trophy.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win on 20 different courses — repeating a course you have already won adds nothing. Choose a fast, stable car, brake before corners instead of inside them, and ride the slipstream on the straights. The activities menu lists your wins, so work through it and skip the courses you hate: 20 is under half the list.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Out-fish Cal in one of his challenges. It is a timing game: watch the tension, reel when the fish runs toward you and back off when it pulls hard, or the line snaps. Cal is a named rival whose challenge surfaces through the fishing activity after you have tried it — fish a few different spots until it appears, then beat his catch.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Play any arcade cabinet to its end screen. Pick the game whose pattern clicks for you — most take only a few minutes to finish. Arcades show on the map once you have found one, and finishing a game here also covers one of the nine activity types for Master of None.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Close out Andy's strand. His missions arrive one at a time — after each one, watch for his next call or a fresh marker on the map. The last mission in a strand is usually its hardest, so arrive stocked. The trophy fires when the strand ends.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Close out Kenton's strand. Missions come one by one, and the game signals the next one with a call or a marker. You cannot jump ahead to the finale — play the strand in order and the trophy lands at the end of his last mission.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Close out Billy's strand. His work is the rougher end of contact jobs — combat and driving in roughly equal measure. A fast car nearby covers the getaways and armour covers the shootouts. The strand ends with this mission, and the trophy with it.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger strands — the ? markers dotted around Leonida. Each one is a short chain of missions for a stranger; the map marks them once you get close, and they stay open in free roam after the story. Clear them region by region while exploring for the 52 areas. There are more than eight strangers in the game, so any strand you dislike can be skipped.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Close out Randy's strand. Take his missions as they arrive and the finale opens after the earlier ones. The last mission is usually a set-piece, so save first and go in prepared — the trophy fires on completion.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Close out Tyrone's strand. His missions unlock one after another and the game points you at each next one. The strand leans on driving and escapes, so keep a quick car in the garage. Finish the finale and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: All 18 meditation spots — and this is the ONE missable trophy, so read this before anything else. The spots are quiet places scattered across Leonida; each one asks you to stop and meditate there, and the game gives you no checklist of its own. Do a spot whenever you pass one while travelling during the story, above all in the early chapters while the map is small, and use this tracker to remember which are done. Finish the story short of 18 and only an earlier save can take you back — never leave this for cleanup.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Track and take down a unique animal for Bret. His hunt is a stranger strand: he names the animal, and you have to find it, close in without spooking it, and land the shot. A scoped rifle, a slow approach downwind and quiet movement are the whole method — animals bolt at noise and speed. Report back to Bret when the hunt is done and the trophy unlocks.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Finish 3 collectible card sets. The cards hide all over Leonida — shops, rooftops, out-of-the-way corners — and a set is done when you hold every card in it. There are more sets than the three you need, so chase the sets whose cards bunch up in districts you already visit. The collection menu shows what you are missing; sweep those districts methodically.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Take WAiNK photos at 100 locations. The spots are photo points across the state — open the WAiNK app at a marked one and shoot. A hundred is a long count, so fold it into everything else: snap a spot whenever you pass one on missions, races and exploration rather than grinding all 100 in one sitting. The app tracks which spots are done, so the last few can be mopped up region by region.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the small tracked goals — stunt jumps, kill counts, driving feats, activity scores and more — and they tick over on their own as you play. The total is cumulative across every type, so 50 usually arrives during a normal playthrough; if you are close at the end, open the challenges list and clear the nearly-finished ones first.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Shake a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you. Build the heat on purpose — stir up trouble in a busy area until four stars show — then break line of sight and move. Your partner has to stay with you, so keep them in the car. Lose the search by hiding in alleys, swapping vehicles, or putting distance between you and the search area until the stars clear. A quieter district gives you a cleaner escape route.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner while keeping your wanted level — the catch is that you must NOT lose the heat. Hit three shops in the same area, fast: rob, get back in the car, drive to the next, and never let the wanted level fall away between robberies. Choose three shops near each other, map the route before the first robbery, and keep your partner beside you the whole time.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Get into 100 different vehicles. The first time you climb into a new one counts — cars, bikes, boats, trucks and the stranger rides all add to the total. The tally climbs fastest when you try whatever you pass instead of sticking to one favourite: hop in for a few seconds, even if you do not keep the ride. Vary your wheels and 100 is most of the way done by the end of a normal playthrough.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop 5 enemies during one Combat Focus. That is the slow-motion aiming mode — fire it when a group is bunched together, and the slowed time gives you room to land five clean shots before it ends. Stage it on purpose: find a mission or gang shootout with five or more enemies close together, wait for them to cluster, then activate and work across them with headshots. A rifle with a large magazine keeps you from reloading mid-focus.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave the airport by air, off the schedule — that is the whole trick. Steal a plane from the tarmac and take off, or get airborne from VCIA any way that skips the terminal. Any aircraft on the field will do: line up on a runway, build speed, and lift off. The trophy fires once you are in the air and clear of the airport.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Handle a Rhino — the military tank that rolls in at high wanted levels. Get the heat up until one deploys, then deal with it: sticky bombs on the rear, a rocket launcher, or drawing it somewhere you can shoot it from cover. One tank is enough; you do not need a fleet. Keep armour ready and an escape vehicle nearby, because a Rhino's cannon ends fights quickly.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: A quiet job: rob a jewelry store without anyone noticing. Move slowly, stay out of the cameras' cones and the staff's line of sight, and take the goods without raising the alarm. If anyone spots you, that attempt is over — walk away and try again. Nights are easier than days, a suppressed weapon helps if a guard wanders too close, and the exit should be planned before you step inside.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and get away clean. Vaults are the big jobs: each takes a plan, a crew approach and a getaway. Do them one at a time across the map instead of back-to-back — the heat afterwards is the hard part, so stash a fast car nearby and know your route out of the district before you go in. Five is the silver, and the payout feeds the money trophies too.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob one armored truck and escape. The trucks patrol the roads — spot one, block it or force it to stop, then crack it open and take the cash. Its guards will fight and the police will come, so choose a spot with a fast way out and a car waiting. One clean robbery and getaway is all it takes.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Set foot in all 52 areas of Leonida. The map keeps track of where you have been — open it, find the districts you have never entered, then drive or fly through them. This pairs with almost everything else: WAiNK spots, the card hunt, drone races and stranger strands all drag you into new corners. Clear the last few deliberately at the end with a grid flight over the state.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Hit one illegal operation for each of the 9 gangs. These are gang-run spots on the map, and each gang holds different turf, so the job takes you across the whole state. Hitting one means fighting that gang's crew and leaving with the goods — go in armed and leave fast. Work the gangs one by one; the trophy fires on the ninth.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Order a cocktail at a bar with a view over Ocean Beach. Head for the waterfront, find a spot looking out over the water, and order — the game notes the moment, not the drink. There is no combat and no timer here, just the beach: sunset is the time the trophy describes, so sit down and let the scene play.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a car through a vehicle showroom's front window and out the other side — the classic GTA exit. Choose a showroom with a clear run-up, build speed, and aim for the glass. The game recognises the smash-and-exit the moment you are back on the street. Pure spectacle, so enjoy it.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bowl at the Kolt & Associates' alley. Pick up a ball and deliver it properly — the trophy is about the follow-through, so play a full game or at least make a real delivery rather than just walking in. Bowling is one of the nine activity types, so it covers a slice of Master of None too.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A shared moment between the two leads that the whole state notices — it comes from a story or partner beat rather than a checklist, so keep playing the story with your partner and it will arrive. If it still has not fired by the late story, look at the partner activities: the mass-appeal moment is something done together, not a solo grind.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Keep making choices — the game counts them, up to 500. Dialogue picks, approach picks in missions, and the small either/or moments across the story and free roam all add up. There is no single trick: play through making choices instead of drifting past them and the count climbs until it fires.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Fail at something, then succeed on the immediate retry — the trophy rewards the comeback, not the failure. The simplest route: take a challenge or activity you can retry on the spot (a race, a shooting challenge, a stunt), miss it once, then pass it on the next attempt. The game counts the retry and the trophy fires.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Stumble into something strange. Leonida hides odd, unscripted moments — strange encounters, weird events and easter eggs tucked into the world — and this trophy fires when you witness one. Wander off the beaten path, look into the strange markers and the places that seem out of place, and let the weirdness find you. There is no checklist for it; it is the game's reward for curiosity.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving car — a drive-by melee, not a gun and not running them over. Crawl along beside a pedestrian so the swing connects, and the trophy fires on the knockdown. A quiet street keeps the cops out of it.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from heists and robberies and cannot be spent as they are — hand them to your contacts a batch at a time. The total is cumulative, so launder every batch you earn instead of letting it pile up. Heists and bank vaults are the fastest source, so this moves in step with the robbery trophies.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across the shops of Leonida. Every shop counts toward one cumulative total — clothes, weapons, car mods, food, everything. It arrives on its own if you buy gear as you go; if you are short near the end, car modifications burn money fastest. Do not hoard cash for this one — spending is the point, and the money trophies want you rich first and generous second.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy the full set of 8 garage properties. They are sold through the in-game property market — each costs money and gives you storage, so they are worth buying as you can afford them. Eight is the whole set; the property listings show which ones you still lack. Save the most expensive for last, when the heist money is flowing, and the trophy fires on the eighth purchase.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Add 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Open the app with a vehicle and register it — ten different ones is the target, so mix it up: cars, bikes and the stranger rides all count as long as they differ. Register as you go and it moves in step with the 100-vehicle discovery trophy.
trophies.name: On the Spot
